newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds sag with rest of Latin America.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds sag with rest of Latin America.

text.p: Argentine bonds ended lower Tuesday as the market was pulled down by declines elsewhere in Latin America.
"We went through some key correction levels," said a trader at a large foreign bank. "There was some nervousness from Mexico," where the peso has recently been under pressure, he said.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 fell $0.20 to 118.80, while Argentina's FRB due 2005 slipped 1/2 to 82-3/4.
The decline of U.S. Treasuries into negative territory in the afternoon added to the fall but prices of Argentine bonds climbed back to close above the session's lows.
Traders said since the market fell through some important levels such as 83 for the FRB, it was likely bonds would firm on Wednesday.
"Ultimately the bond market is firm. And it is not worrying, but healthy, that there is profit-taking," said another trader.
The fact that Tuesday's profit-taking took place amid slim trading volumes made the decline even less important, said an analyst at a large foreign bank.

Traders said the issuance of 250 million pesos in 91-day treasury bills (Letes) at a cut-off yield of 7.21 percent and another $500 million in 364-day Letes at 6.75 percent at today's bill auction had no impact on the market. "The bills' sale was positive but it was neither good nor bad for the bond market," said the first trader.
On Wednesday, the market is expected to take its cue from the release of U.S. consumer price figures, said traders.
In the money markets, call money rates rose to 6.75 percent from 6.55 percent.
